chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: To provide additional information about HTML elements, you need to get familiar with attributes.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: Attributes can provide more details about an element.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: They're always specified in the start tag of an element and usually coming name slash value pairs like this.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: One type of attribute is HR-EF like in this example.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: Links are defined with the A tag and the link address or URL is specified in the HR-EF attribute.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: Another type of attribute is SRC. We call that source like in this example.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: HTML images are defined with the IMG tag and the image source or URL is defined by the SRC attribute.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: Images in HTML have a set of size attributes. These correspond to the width and height of an image.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: For instance, an image size with a width of 500 equates to 500 pixels wide.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: If you change the width to 300, the image will become smaller.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: The style attribute is used to specify the look or style of an element. This is called CSS.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: And you'll learn about that in another chapter. For now, you just need to know that CSS allows you to change colors, sizes and set the layout of your page.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: The language of the document can be declared in the HTML tag with the Lang attribute.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: This is important for screen readers and search engines.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: The title attribute specifies a title for an element.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: The value of this title is displayed as a tooltip when you move the mouse over the element.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: Double quotes around attribute values are the most common but single quotes can also be used.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: And sometimes you actually have to use both. For instance, if an attribute value contains double quotes, it is necessary to use single quotes around it or vice versa.

chunks.title: Attributes
chunks.text: So remember, if you want to change something about an element, you will probably need an attribute.
